title: How to surpass no-go limits in Gaussian quantum error correction and entangled Gaussian state distillation

candidates.error_location: Eq. (17) and the sentence following it (Application paragraph)
candidates.claim_content: The paper states that the GKP two-mode-squeezing (TMS) code applied to an additive Gaussian channel of noise variance \sigma^2 gives logical variance \sigma_L^2 (their Eq. (15)), and that when the channel is first noise-polarized (so that the good mode has variance e^{-2r}\sigma^2) the logical variance becomes \sigma_L^2 = e^{-2r}\frac{2\sigma^2}{\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{4r + \ln\frac{\pi^{1.5}}{2\sigma^4}} (their Eq. (16)). It then asserts that 'this concatenation is useful when' 4/\ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4)) + 1 < e^{4r}, and immediately afterwards that 'this concatenation always yields benefits for r > 0'. Writing L := \ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4)), the comparison \sigma_L^2(\text{polarized}) < \sigma_L^2(\text{unpolarized}) with the square-root form of Eqs. (15)-(16) is e^{-2r}\sqrt{L+4r} < \sqrt{L}, i.e. L + 4r < e^{4r}L, i.e. 1 + 4r/L < e^{4r}.
candidates.suspected_defect: The derived condition is 1 + 4r/L < e^{4r} (numerator 4r), but the paper prints 1 + 4/L < e^{4r} (numerator 4). Moreover, as printed, the condition is violated for all sufficiently small r > 0 (LHS tends to 1 + 4/L > 1 while e^{4r} tends to 1), which directly contradicts the following sentence claiming the concatenation 'always yields benefits for r > 0'. With the corrected 4r/L the claim holds precisely when L > 1.

candidates.error_location: Application paragraph, numerical condition after Eq. (17)
candidates.claim_content: The paper claims that the numerical threshold on the input noise variance for the GKP concatenation to always help is \sigma^2 < \pi^3/(4\sqrt{2e}), and says this number is approximately 1.012. Here e is Euler's number and \pi = 3.14159...; the threshold arises from requiring \ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4)) > 1, i.e. \pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4) > e, i.e. \sigma^4 < \pi^{1.5}/(2e), i.e. \sigma^2 < \pi^{3/4}/\sqrt{2e}.
candidates.suspected_defect: Numerically \pi^3/(4\sqrt{2e}) = 31.006/9.327 = 3.324, not 1.012. The value 1.012 corresponds to \pi^{3/4}/\sqrt{2e} = 2.3597/2.3317 = 1.012, which is the quantity that actually follows from the condition \ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4)) > 1. Hence the printed closed form and the quoted numerical value are inconsistent.

candidates.claim_content: Eq. (15) gives the logical noise variance of the GKP two-mode squeezing code on an additive Gaussian channel with noise variance \sigma^2 as \sigma_L^2 = (2\sigma^2/\sqrt{\pi})\,\ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4)) (no square root). Eq. (16) is obtained by applying the same formula to a polarized channel whose good-mode variance is e^{-2r}\sigma^2, and reads \sigma_L^2 = e^{-2r}(2\sigma^2/\sqrt{\pi})\sqrt{4r + \ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4))} (with a square root). Substituting \sigma^2 \to e^{-2r}\sigma^2 into Eq. (15) gives (2e^{-2r}\sigma^2/\sqrt{\pi})\,[4r + \ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4))], with no square root.
candidates.suspected_defect: Eqs. (15) and (16) are mutually inconsistent: one has the logarithm, the other the square root of the same logarithm, even though (16) is supposed to be (15) evaluated at the reduced variance e^{-2r}\sigma^2. One of the two expressions must be wrong, and the subsequent usefulness condition (Eq. (17), involving e^{4r}) is only compatible with the square-root version.

candidates.exact_quote: Let $f_i : \hat{q}_i, \hat{p}_i \mapsto \hat{q}_i, -\hat{p}_i$ be a function describing the action of partial transpose on the $i$-th mode in the Heisenberg picture for $i \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $\hat{W}^{T_i}(\hat{x}) = f_i(\hat{W}(\hat{x})) = \hat{W}(f_i(\hat{x}))$.
candidates.claim_content: Setting: bosonic modes with q = (a+a^\dagger)/\sqrt2, p = (a-a^\dagger)/(i\sqrt2), [q,p] = i. Transposition in the Fock basis satisfies a^T = a^\dagger, hence q^T = q and p^T = -p, and transposition is an ANTI-automorphism: (AB)^T = B^T A^T; for partial transposition on mode i, (XY)^{T_i} \neq Y^{T_i}X^{T_i} in general. The paper claims that for any operator \hat W that is a function of the quadrature vector \hat x, the partial transpose on mode i is obtained by the substitution p_i \to -p_i, i.e. \hat W^{T_i}(\hat x) = \hat W(f_i(\hat x)) with f_i: (q_i,p_i) \mapsto (q_i,-p_i).
candidates.suspected_defect: The substitution map f_i is treated as an algebra automorphism, but (i) it does not preserve the canonical commutation relation ([q_i,-p_i] = -i \neq i), and (ii) transposition reverses operator order. For \hat W = e^{-i\hat H t} with \hat H a sum of non-commuting terms, (e^{-i\hat H t})^{T_i} is generally NOT equal to e^{-i\hat H(f_i(\hat x))t}. Consequently Eq. (12), which asserts (\hat W(f_i(\hat x)))^\dagger \hat x_j \hat x_k \hat W(f_i(\hat x)) = f_i(\hat W(\hat x)^\dagger f_i(\hat x_j \hat x_k)\hat W(\hat x)), does not follow, and the resulting covariance rule \tilde M_i = Z_i M Z_i is unjustified for the operator-level partial transpose \hat W^{T_i}. (The rule Z_i M Z_i is valid for the different object T_i \circ \Phi \circ T_i, not for \rho \mapsto \hat W^{T_i}\rho(\hat W^{T_i})^\dagger.)

candidates.error_location: Lemma 4 / Theorem 5 (use of the non-symplectic matrix \tilde M_i = Z_i M Z_i)
candidates.exact_quote: In general, $\tilde{M}_i$ is not symplectic since $Z_i$ is not symplectic.
candidates.claim_content: Conventions: \hat x = (q_1,p_1,q_2,p_2); \Omega = \Omega_1 \oplus \Omega_1 with \Omega_1 = [[0,-1],[1,0]]; Z = diag(1,-1); Z_2 = I \oplus Z; the balanced beam splitter has symplectic matrix B = (1/\sqrt2)[[I,I],[-I,I]]. The paper defines B_i: \mathcal G^{M,N} \mapsto \mathcal G^{Z_iMZ_i, Z_iNZ_i} and uses B_2(\mathcal G^{B}) and B_2(\mathcal G^{B^T}) as physically implementable operations (via CV gate teleportation) inside the composite channel of Theorem 5, and treats their action on covariance matrices as \gamma \mapsto \tilde M \gamma \tilde M^T. Claim to check: (a) \tilde M = Z_2 B Z_2 = (1/\sqrt2)[[I,Z],[-Z,I]] is not symplectic, i.e. \tilde M^T \Omega \tilde M \neq \Omega (the (1,1) block evaluates to \Omega_1 + Z\Omega_1 Z = 0); hence there is no Gaussian unitary with this symplectic matrix and \rho \mapsto \hat B^{T_2}\rho(\hat B^{T_2})^\dagger is not trace-preserving, so the covariance transformation \gamma \mapsto \tilde M \gamma \tilde M^T (which presupposes a unitary/trace-preserving map) is invalid. (b) The claimed output noise matrix N^{polar} = \sigma^2 diag(e^{-2r}I, e^{2r}I) satisfies N^{polar}/\sigma^2 not symplectic (its \Omega-congruence gives diag(e^{-4r}\Omega_1, e^{4r}\Omega_1)), hence it cannot be written as \sigma^2 S S^T for any symplectic S, i.e. it is unreachable from two i.i.d. channels with N = \sigma^2 I_4 by any Gaussian-unitary encoder/decoder pair.
candidates.suspected_defect: The whole noise-polarization result rests on treating a non-symplectic (hence non-physical, non-trace-preserving) matrix transformation as an implementable Gaussian operation, and on applying the covariance-matrix update rule \gamma \mapsto M\gamma M^T + N outside its domain of validity (unitary/CP-trace-preserving Gaussian maps). The non-symplecticity shown in (a) and the non-reachability shown in (b) indicate the construction is not physically realizable as claimed.

candidates.exact_quote: \gamma(\rho) \xrightarrow{\hat{W}^{T_i}(\hat{x})} Z_i M Z_i \gamma(\rho) Z_i M Z_i + Z_i N Z_i.
candidates.claim_content: Context: a Gaussian operation \mathcal G^{M,N} acts on covariance matrices by \gamma \mapsto M\gamma M^T + N (Eq. (2)), with M, N real 2n x 2n matrices, N symmetric PSD. Lemma 4 states that the partial transpose with respect to mode i is \mathcal G^{\tilde M_i, \tilde N_i} with \tilde M_i = Z_i M Z_i, \tilde N_i = Z_i N Z_i and Z_i = I^{\oplus i-1} \oplus Z \oplus I^{\oplus n-i}, Z = diag(1,-1). Eq. (13) writes the resulting covariance update as Z_i M Z_i \gamma Z_i M Z_i + Z_i N Z_i.
candidates.suspected_defect: The second factor is missing a transpose: consistency with Eq. (2) and with the lemma's own statement requires \gamma \mapsto (Z_iMZ_i)\gamma(Z_iMZ_i)^T + Z_iNZ_i = Z_iMZ_i\,\gamma\,Z_iM^TZ_i + Z_iNZ_i. As written, Eq. (13) is only correct for symmetric M.

candidates.claim_content: Definitions used by the paper: |\zeta_{EPR}\rangle \propto \sum_n |n\rangle|n\rangle (infinitely squeezed EPR); Lemma 2 (CV bouncing): (\hat I \otimes \hat W)|\zeta_{EPR}\rangle = (\hat W^T \otimes \hat I)|\zeta_{EPR}\rangle, whose dual form is \langle\zeta_{EPR}|(\hat A \otimes \hat I) = \langle\zeta_{EPR}|(\hat I \otimes \hat A^T); the paper's own transpose rule for displacements: \hat D^T(\alpha) = (\hat D^\dagger(\alpha))^* = \hat D(-\alpha^*); and \mu_\pm := \sqrt2 (q_1 \pm i p_2) with q_1, p_2 real, so \mu_+^* = \mu_-. Applying the dual bouncing rule to the mode-1 operator \hat D_1^\dagger(\mu_+/2) = \hat D_1(-\mu_+/2) moves it to mode 2 as (\hat D(-\mu_+/2))^T = \hat D(-(-\mu_+/2)^*) = \hat D(\mu_+^*/2) = \hat D(\mu_-/2).
candidates.suspected_defect: After the bounce the mode-2 operator is \hat D_2(\mu_-/2), which multiplied by the already present \hat D_2^\dagger(\mu_-/2) gives the identity (up to a phase), so the claimed result \langle\zeta|\hat D_2(-\mu_-)|\zeta\rangle does not follow; the stated chain would in fact make the Kraus operator outcome-independent (pure teleportation with no displacement), which is physically wrong. There is a sign/convention inconsistency between (A3) and (A4).

candidates.claim_content: Using Lemma 2 in the form (\hat W \otimes \hat I)|\zeta_{EPR}\rangle_{2,3} = (\hat I \otimes \hat W^T)|\zeta_{EPR}\rangle_{2,3} (equivalent to the stated (\hat I \otimes \hat W)|\zeta\rangle = (\hat W^T \otimes \hat I)|\zeta\rangle since (\hat W^T)^T = \hat W), together with the paper's rule \hat D^T(\alpha) = \hat D(-\alpha^*) and \mu_\pm = \sqrt2(q_1 \pm i p_2) with q_1,p_2 real (so \mu_-^* = \mu_+), moving \hat D_2(-\mu_-) acting on the first slot of |\zeta_{EPR}\rangle_{2,3} to mode 3 gives (\hat D(-\mu_-))^T = \hat D(-(-\mu_-)^*) = \hat D(\mu_-^*) = \hat D(\mu_+).
candidates.suspected_defect: The bounce yields \hat D_3(+\mu_+), not \hat D_3(-\mu_+) as printed; the sign of the measurement-dependent displacement (and hence of the required recovery operation \hat D_3(\mu) in Fig. 1 and Eq. (6)) is inconsistent with the stated transpose rule.

candidates.error_location: Appendix B, definition of the displacement operator
candidates.exact_quote: Recall that the displacement operator \(\hat{D}_j(\alpha) = e^{i\sqrt{2} \left( \mathrm{Im}\{\alpha\} \hat{q}_j + \mathrm{Re}\{\alpha\} \hat{p}_j \right) }\).
candidates.claim_content: The paper defines \hat D(\alpha) := e^{\alpha \hat a^\dagger - \alpha^* \hat a}, with \hat q = (\hat a + \hat a^\dagger)/\sqrt2 and \hat p = (\hat a - \hat a^\dagger)/(i\sqrt2), i.e. \hat a = (\hat q + i \hat p)/\sqrt2. Substituting gives \alpha \hat a^\dagger - \alpha^* \hat a = [(\alpha-\alpha^*)\hat q - i(\alpha+\alpha^*)\hat p]/\sqrt2 = i\sqrt2(\mathrm{Im}\{\alpha\}\hat q - \mathrm{Re}\{\alpha\}\hat p).
candidates.suspected_defect: The paper writes +Re{\alpha}\hat p_j in the exponent, whereas the definition \hat D(\alpha)=e^{\alpha a^\dagger - \alpha^* a} with the paper's own quadrature conventions gives -Re{\alpha}\hat p_j. This sign error propagates into Eqs. (B17), (C5) and (C6).

candidates.claim_content: The paper defines the two-mode squeezer as \hat S_{j,k}(r) := e^{r(\hat a_j \hat a_k - \hat a_j^\dagger \hat a_k^\dagger)} and states that applying it to the vacuum yields |\zeta_r\rangle_{1,2} = (1/\cosh r)\sum_{n} \tanh^n(r)|n\rangle_1|n\rangle_2. The standard disentangling identity gives e^{r(ab - a^\dagger b^\dagger)}|0,0\rangle = (1/\cosh r)\sum_n (-\tanh r)^n |n,n\rangle.
candidates.suspected_defect: With the paper's own sign convention for \hat S_{j,k}(r), the vacuum output carries (-\tanh r)^n, not (\tanh r)^n; Eq. (4) corresponds to \hat S_{j,k}(-r)|0,0\rangle. This sign slip also feeds into the Appendix G fidelity expansion, which uses \tanh^{m'+n'}(r)/\cosh^2(r).

candidates.error_location: Gaussian quantum information processing section, symplectic matrix of the two-mode squeezer
candidates.claim_content: The paper defines single-mode squeezer \hat S_j(r) := e^{r(\hat a_j^2 - \hat a_j^{\dagger 2})/2} with symplectic matrix S_j(r) = diag(e^{-r}, e^{r}) (which corresponds to the Heisenberg rule \hat U^\dagger \hat x \hat U = M \hat x), and the two-mode squeezer \hat S_{j,k}(r) := e^{r(\hat a_j \hat a_k - \hat a_j^\dagger \hat a_k^\dagger)} with symplectic matrix S_{j,k}(r) = [[\cosh r\, I, \sinh r\, Z],[\sinh r\, Z, \cosh r\, I]], Z = diag(1,-1). Direct computation gives \hat S_{j,k}^\dagger(r)\hat a_j \hat S_{j,k}(r) = \hat a_j \cosh r - \hat a_k^\dagger \sinh r, hence q_j \mapsto \cosh r\, q_j - \sinh r\, q_k and p_j \mapsto \cosh r\, p_j + \sinh r\, p_k, i.e. M = [[\cosh r\, I, -\sinh r\, Z],[-\sinh r\, Z, \cosh r\, I]].
candidates.suspected_defect: Under the same Heisenberg convention that makes S_j(r) = diag(e^{-r},e^{r}) correct for \hat S_j(r), the operator \hat S_{j,k}(r) corresponds to the matrix with -\sinh r Z off-diagonal blocks, i.e. to the paper's S_{j,k}(-r). The operator-to-matrix correspondence for the two-mode squeezer therefore carries an inconsistent sign relative to the single-mode case.

candidates.claim_content: Definitions: |\Psi_0\rangle := |\zeta_r\rangle_{i,j} \otimes |\psi\rangle_{k_1,\dots,k_n} (a normalized state, since |\zeta_r\rangle is a finitely squeezed, normalized TMSV), \rho_0 = |\Psi_0\rangle\langle\Psi_0|, |\Psi_L\rangle := (\hat I_i \otimes \hat W_{j,k_1})|\Psi_0\rangle, |\Psi_R\rangle := (\hat W^{T_i}_{i,k_1} \otimes \hat I_j)|\Psi_0\rangle, \rho_L = |\Psi_L\rangle\langle\Psi_L|, \rho_R = |\Psi_R\rangle\langle\Psi_R|, and \hat V := (\hat W^{T_i}_{i,k_1} \otimes \hat I_j)^\dagger(\hat I_i \otimes \hat W_{j,k_1}). The paper asserts that the fidelity between \rho_L and \rho_R equals |\mathrm{tr}(\rho_0 \hat V)|^2.
candidates.suspected_defect: The partial transpose \hat W^{T_i} of a unitary \hat W is in general not unitary (for the balanced beam splitter the associated matrix Z_2 B Z_2 is not even symplectic), so |\Psi_R\rangle is not normalized and \rho_R is not a normalized state. The fidelity should then be |\langle\Psi_R|\Psi_L\rangle|^2/(\langle\Psi_L|\Psi_L\rangle\langle\Psi_R|\Psi_R\rangle); the unnormalized expression |\mathrm{tr}(\rho_0\hat V)|^2 is not a fidelity and need not approach 1 as r \to \infty.

candidates.error_location: Main text, paragraph after Lemma 3 (implementation of the partial transpose by gate teleportation with displacement recovery)
candidates.exact_quote: Moreover, by combining Lemma 1 and Lemma 3, we can effectively implement the partial transpose of a balanced beam splitter through CV gate teleportation with recovery by displacement operators.
candidates.claim_content: The recovery-operator analysis (Eq. (7) and Appendix B, Lemma 7) proves that for a gate \hat W_{j,k} = e^{-i\hat H_{j,k}t} with \hat H_{j,k} a real linear combination of \{\hat I, \hat q_j, \hat p_j, \hat q_k, \hat p_k, \hat q_j\hat q_k, \hat q_j \hat p_k, \hat p_j \hat q_k, \hat p_j \hat p_k\} (hence \hat W unitary), the recovery operator \hat W_{3,4}\hat D_3(\mu)\hat W_{3,4}^\dagger reduces to a product of displacement operators. The paper then applies this conclusion to \hat W = \hat B^{T_2}_{j,k}, the partial transpose of the balanced beam splitter.
candidates.suspected_defect: Lemma 7 / Lemma 1 are proved only for unitary gates generated by Hermitian quadratic Hamiltonians (the derivation uses \hat W \hat D \hat W^\dagger with \hat W^\dagger = \hat W^{-1} and the Heisenberg evolution of quadratures). The operator \hat B^{T_2} has the purported matrix Z_2BZ_2, which is not symplectic, so \hat B^{T_2} is not a Gaussian unitary and the recovery formula \hat W \hat D(\mu)\hat W^\dagger (a product of displacements) is invoked outside the hypotheses under which it was established.

candidates.error_location: Gaussian quantum information processing section, definition of the covariance matrix
candidates.exact_quote: the (j, k)-th entry of γ(ρ) is γ(ρ)ⱼ,ₖ = tr(ρx̂ⱼx̂ₖ)
candidates.claim_content: The paper sets \hbar = 1, [\hat q,\hat p] = i, considers zero-mean Gaussian states, and defines the covariance matrix entrywise by \gamma(\rho)_{j,k} = \mathrm{tr}(\rho\,\hat x_j \hat x_k). It subsequently treats \gamma as a real symmetric matrix transforming as \gamma \mapsto M\gamma M^T + N with N real symmetric PSD, and uses f_i(\gamma(\rho)) = Z_i\gamma(\rho)Z_i in the proof of Lemma 4.
candidates.suspected_defect: With the non-symmetrized product, \gamma_{1,2} = \mathrm{tr}(\rho\,\hat q\hat p) and \gamma_{2,1} = \mathrm{tr}(\rho\,\hat p\hat q) differ by i (since [\hat q,\hat p]=i), so \gamma is neither real nor symmetric; e.g. for the vacuum \gamma = I/2 + (i/2)\Omega. The standard definition requires the symmetrized (anticommutator) form. All statements that treat \gamma as real symmetric (and the identification of N with a real symmetric PSD noise matrix) are therefore based on an inconsistent definition.
